chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sam'ah, from more than one, all of them, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial animal (hady), what the one who offers it eats from it during his 'umrah al-tamattu' and otherwise, so he said: 'Just as he eats from his sacrificial animal [in the case of qiran or individual hajj].'

key_terms.أَبَانٍ: Aban ibn Tammam, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith sources
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ الل: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah al-Hamadani, a key narrator
key_terms.مُتْعَتِهِ: The 'Umrah al-Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a pilgrim eating from their sacrificial animal during Umrah al-Tamattu?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the pilgrim performing *Umrah al-Tamattu'* consumes the sacrificial animal (*hady*) under the same general conditions as other Hajj forms, rejecting any notion of unique dietary restrictions for this specific ritual. This ruling underscores the principle of uniformity in the legal treatment of sacrificial meat across different Hajj types, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the purification and distribution of *hady*. The hadith is transmitted through a strong chain (*isnad*) involving prominent narrators like Aban ibn Taghlib, reflecting the early juristic consensus on the matter.
